# Incident Response Standard

## 1. Purpose

This standard establishes requirements for incident response capabilities at Acme Health to ensure the organization can effectively prepare for, detect, respond to, and recover from security and privacy incidents in compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and industry frameworks.

## 2. Scope

This standard applies to all information systems, personnel, and processes involved in the detection, reporting, response to, and recovery from security and privacy incidents affecting Acme Health operations and the protected health information under its control.

## 3. Roles and Responsibilities

### 3.1 Designated Official

Acme Health shall designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the incident response policy and procedures. [NIST 800-53 IR-1 | FedRAMP IR-1 | ARC-AMPE IR-1]

### 3.2 Information System Security Officer (ISSO)

The applicable Information System Security Officer (ISSO) shall coordinate incident response activities, including forensic malware analysis, and shall review and approve the incident response plan. [ARC-AMPE IR-4 | ARC-AMPE IR-8]

### 3.3 Business Owner

The Business Owner shall approve the incident response plan. [ARC-AMPE IR-8]

### 3.4 Incident Response Personnel

Acme Health shall explicitly designate responsibility for incident response to [Assignment: organization-defined entities, personnel, or roles]. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8]

Acme Health shall explicitly designate responsibility for incident response to the applicable Information System Security Officer (ISSO), approved by the Business Owner. [ARC-AMPE IR-8]

## 4. Incident Response Policy

### 4.1 Policy Development and Dissemination

Acme Health shall develop, document, and disseminate to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] an incident response policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. [NIST 800-53 IR-1 | FedRAMP IR-1 | ARC-AMPE IR-1]

Acme Health shall develop, document, and disseminate to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] an organization-level incident response policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and is consistent with applicable laws, Executive Orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. [ARC-AMPE IR-1]

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures to address security incidents. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(6)(i)]

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(1)(i)]

### 4.2 Procedures

Acme Health shall develop, document, and disseminate to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] procedures to facilitate the implementation of the incident response policy and the associated incident response controls. [NIST 800-53 IR-1 | FedRAMP IR-1 | ARC-AMPE IR-1]

### 4.3 Policy and Procedure Review and Update

Acme Health shall review and update the incident response policy [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]. [NIST 800-53 IR-1 | FedRAMP IR-1]

Acme Health shall review and update the incident response policy at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events. [ARC-AMPE IR-1]

Acme Health shall review and update the incident response procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]. [NIST 800-53 IR-1 | FedRAMP IR-1]

Acme Health shall review and update the incident response procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events. [ARC-AMPE IR-1]

### 4.4 FedRAMP Requirements

Acme Health shall follow the FedRAMP Incident Evaluation and Communication rules. [FedRAMP IR-1]

## 5. Incident Response Training

### 5.1 Training Requirements

Acme Health shall provide incident response training to system users consistent with assigned roles and responsibilities within [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of assuming an incident response role or responsibility or acquiring system access. [NIST 800-53 IR-2 | FedRAMP IR-2]

Acme Health shall provide incident response training to system users consistent with assigned roles and responsibilities within one (1) month of assuming an incident response role or responsibility or acquiring system access. [ARC-AMPE IR-2]

Acme Health shall provide incident response training when required by system changes. [NIST 800-53 IR-2 | FedRAMP IR-2 | ARC-AMPE IR-2]

Acme Health shall provide incident response training [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] thereafter. [NIST 800-53 IR-2 | FedRAMP IR-2]

Acme Health shall provide incident response training within one (1) year thereafter. [ARC-AMPE IR-2]

### 5.2 Training Content

Incident response training shall include privacy education and awareness training associated with sending sensitive information (e.g., confidential, proprietary, financial, and or Personally Identifiable Information [PII]). [ARC-AMPE IR-2]

Incident response training shall include how to recognize when sensitive information such as PII is involved so that personnel can coordinate with the designated privacy official. [ARC-AMPE IR-2]

Incident response training shall include how to identify and respond to a breach, including the organization's process for reporting a breach. [NIST 800-53 IR-2(3) | ARC-AMPE IR-2(3)]

### 5.3 Training Content Review and Update

Acme Health shall review and update incident response training content [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events]. [NIST 800-53 IR-2 | FedRAMP IR-2]

Acme Health shall review and update incident response training content every one (1) year and following defined events/incidents. [ARC-AMPE IR-2]

### 5.4 Training Records

Acme Health shall formally maintain and record personnel participating in incident response training. [ARC-AMPE IR-2]

### 5.5 Simulated Events

Acme Health shall incorporate simulated events into incident response training to facilitate the required response by personnel in crisis situations. [NIST 800-53 IR-2(1) High | FedRAMP IR-2(1)]

### 5.6 Automated Training Environment

Acme Health shall provide an incident response training environment using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]. [NIST 800-53 IR-2(2) High | FedRAMP IR-2(2)]

## 6. Incident Response Testing

### 6.1 Testing Requirements

Acme Health shall test the effectiveness of the incident response capability for the system [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] using the following tests: [Assignment: organization-defined tests]. [NIST 800-53 IR-3 Moderate, High | FedRAMP IR-3]

Acme Health shall test the effectiveness of the incident response capability for the system within every one (1) year using appropriate organization-defined tests to determine the incident response effectiveness, and document the results. [ARC-AMPE IR-3]

### 6.2 Coordination of Testing

Acme Health shall coordinate incident response testing with organizational elements responsible for related plans. [NIST 800-53 IR-3(2) Moderate, High | FedRAMP IR-3(2) | ARC-AMPE IR-3(2)]

### 6.3 Automated Testing

Acme Health shall test the incident response capability using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]. [NIST 800-53 IR-3(1)]

### 6.4 Continuous Improvement

Acme Health shall determine the effectiveness of incident response processes; continuously improve incident response processes; and provide incident response measures and metrics that are accurate, consistent, and in a reproducible format. [NIST 800-53 IR-3(3)]

## 7. Incident Handling

### 7.1 Incident Handling Capability

Acme Health shall implement an incident handling capability for incidents that is consistent with the incident response plan and includes preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery. [NIST 800-53 IR-4 | FedRAMP IR-4 | ARC-AMPE IR-4]

Acme Health shall coordinate incident handling activities with contingency planning activities. [NIST 800-53 IR-4 | FedRAMP IR-4 | ARC-AMPE IR-4]

Acme Health shall incorporate lessons learned from ongoing incident handling activities into incident response procedures, training, and testing, and implement the resulting changes accordingly. [NIST 800-53 IR-4 | FedRAMP IR-4 | ARC-AMPE IR-4]

Acme Health shall ensure the rigor, intensity, scope, and results of incident handling activities are comparable and predictable across the organization. [NIST 800-53 IR-4 | FedRAMP IR-4 | ARC-AMPE IR-4]

### 7.2 Incident Documentation

Acme Health shall identify and respond to suspected or known security incidents; mitigate, to the extent practicable, harmful effects of security incidents that are known to the covered entity or business associate; and document security incidents and their outcomes. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(6)(ii)]

Acme Health shall document relevant information related to a security and privacy incident in accordance with the current organization Incident Handling and Breach Notification Standard and Procedures and inclusive of CMS reporting requirements and timelines. [ARC-AMPE IR-4]

Acme Health shall maintain in the system Incident Response Plan contact information for individuals within the organization and CMS who have incident handling responsibilities. [ARC-AMPE IR-4]

### 7.3 Evidence Preservation

Acme Health shall preserve evidence through technical means, including secured storage of evidence media and write protection of evidence media, using sound forensics processes and utilities that support legal requirements, and determine and follow a chain of custody for forensic evidence. [ARC-AMPE IR-4]

### 7.4 Vulnerability Response

Acme Health shall identify vulnerability exploited during a security and privacy incident and implement safeguards to reduce risk and vulnerability exploit exposure, including isolating or disconnecting systems. [ARC-AMPE IR-4]

### 7.5 Activity Monitoring

Acme Health shall implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D)]

### 7.6 Automated Support

Acme Health shall support the incident handling process using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(1) Moderate, High | FedRAMP IR-4(1)]

### 7.7 Dynamic Reconfiguration

Acme Health shall include the following types of dynamic reconfiguration for [Assignment: organization-defined system components] as part of the incident response capability: [Assignment: organization-defined types of dynamic reconfiguration]. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(2) | FedRAMP IR-4(2)]

### 7.8 Continuity of Operations

Acme Health shall identify [Assignment: organization-defined classes of incidents] and take the following actions in response to those incidents to ensure continuation of organizational mission and business functions: [Assignment: organization-defined actions]. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(3)]

Acme Health shall identify classes of incidents and take actions in response to those incidents to ensure continuation of organizational missions and business functions, including graceful degradation; information system shutdown; fall back to manual mode/alternative technology whereby the system operates differently; employing deceptive measures; alternate information flows; or operating in a mode that is reserved solely for when systems are under attack. [ARC-AMPE IR-4(3)]

### 7.9 Organization-Wide Perspective

Acme Health shall correlate incident information and individual incident responses to achieve an organization-wide perspective on incident awareness and response. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(4) High | FedRAMP IR-4(4)]

### 7.10 Automatic Disabling

Acme Health shall implement a configurable capability to automatically disable the system if [Assignment: organization-defined security violations] are detected. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(5)]

### 7.11 Insider Threats

Acme Health shall implement an incident handling capability for incidents involving insider threats. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(6) | FedRAMP IR-4(6) | ARC-AMPE IR-4(6)]

Acme Health shall coordinate an incident handling capability for insider threats that includes the following organizational entities [Assignment: organization-defined entities]. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(7)]

### 7.12 Cross-Organization Coordination

Acme Health shall coordinate with [Assignment: organization-defined external organizations] to correlate and share [Assignment: organization-defined incident information] to achieve a cross-organization perspective on incident awareness and more effective incident responses. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(8)]

### 7.13 Dynamic Response Capabilities

Acme Health shall employ [Assignment: organization-defined dynamic response capabilities] to respond to incidents. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(9)]

### 7.14 Supply Chain Incidents

Acme Health shall coordinate incident handling activities involving supply chain events with other organizations involved in the supply chain. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(10)]

### 7.15 Integrated Incident Response Team

Acme Health shall establish and maintain an integrated incident response team that can be deployed to any location identified by the organization in [Assignment: organization-defined time period]. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(11) High | FedRAMP IR-4(11)]

### 7.16 Malicious Code Analysis

Acme Health shall analyze malicious code and/or other residual artifacts remaining in the system after the incident. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(12)]

### 7.17 Behavioral Analysis

Acme Health shall analyze anomalous or suspected adversarial behavior in or related to [Assignment: organization-defined environments or resources]. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(13)]

### 7.18 Security Operations Center

Acme Health shall establish and maintain a security operations center. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(14)]

### 7.19 Public Relations

Acme Health shall manage public relations associated with an incident and employ measures to repair the reputation of the organization. [NIST 800-53 IR-4(15)]

## 8. Incident Monitoring

### 8.1 Tracking and Documentation

Acme Health shall track and document incidents. [NIST 800-53 IR-5 | FedRAMP IR-5 | ARC-AMPE IR-5]

### 8.2 Automated Tracking

Acme Health shall track incidents and collect and analyze incident information using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]. [NIST 800-53 IR-5(1) High | FedRAMP IR-5(1)]

## 9. Incident Reporting

### 9.1 Internal Reporting Requirements

Acme Health shall require personnel to report suspected incidents to the organizational incident response capability within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]. [NIST 800-53 IR-6 | FedRAMP IR-6]

Acme Health shall require personnel to report suspected incidents to the organizational incident response capability within the timeframe established in the current organization Incident Handling Procedure. [ARC-AMPE IR-6]

### 9.2 External Reporting Requirements

Acme Health shall report incident information to [Assignment: organization-defined authorities]. [NIST 800-53 IR-6 | FedRAMP IR-6 | ARC-AMPE IR-6]

Acme Health shall report suspected incident information to CMS within the timeframe established in the organization Incident Handling Procedure and applicable current legally binding agreements. [ARC-AMPE IR-6]

State AE must report potential or confirmed security incidents within one (1) hour of discovery by completing the CMS ACA Security and Privacy Incident Response Template and notifying the CMS IT Service Desk. [ARC-AMPE IR-6]

### 9.3 Automated Reporting

Acme Health shall report incidents using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]. [NIST 800-53 IR-6(1) Moderate, High | FedRAMP IR-6(1) | ARC-AMPE IR-6(1)]

### 9.4 Vulnerability Reporting

Acme Health shall report system vulnerabilities associated with reported incidents to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]. [NIST 800-53 IR-6(2)]

### 9.5 Supply Chain Coordination

Acme Health shall provide incident information to the provider of the product or service and other organizations involved in the supply chain or supply chain governance for systems or system components related to the incident. [NIST 800-53 IR-6(3) Moderate, High | FedRAMP IR-6(3)]

### 9.6 Business Associate Reporting

Business associates must report to the covered entity any security incident of which it becomes aware, including breaches of unsecured protected health information. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.314(a)(2)(i)]

Business associate contracts with subcontractors must require the subcontractor to report security incidents to the business associate. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.314(a)(2)(iii)]

### 9.7 Plan Sponsor Reporting

Plan sponsors must report to the group health plan any security incident of which it becomes aware. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.314(b)(2)]

## 10. Incident Response Assistance

### 10.1 Incident Response Support Resource

Acme Health shall provide an incident response support resource, integral to the organizational incident response capability, that offers advice and assistance to users of the system for the handling and reporting of incidents. [NIST 800-53 IR-7 | FedRAMP IR-7 | ARC-AMPE IR-7]

Incident response assistance for incidents involving Personally Identifiable Information (PII) includes use of the forensic, technical, policy, and legal expertise of the organization's Information Assurance Officers/Managers, Privacy Officers, Legal Counsel, and external or internal Information Technology help desks. [ARC-AMPE IR-7]

### 10.2 Automated Assistance

Acme Health shall increase the availability of incident response information and support using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]. [NIST 800-53 IR-7(1) Moderate, High | FedRAMP IR-7(1) | ARC-AMPE IR-7(1)]

### 10.3 External Coordination

Acme Health shall establish a direct, cooperative relationship between the organization's incident response capability and external providers of system protection capability, and identify organizational incident response team members to the external providers. [NIST 800-53 IR-7(2) | ARC-AMPE IR-7(2)]

## 11. Incident Response Plan

### 11.1 Plan Development

Acme Health shall develop an incident response plan that provides the organization with a roadmap for implementing its incident response capability. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8 | ARC-AMPE IR-8]

Acme Health shall develop an incident response plan that describes the structure and organization of the incident response capability. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8 | ARC-AMPE IR-8]

Acme Health shall develop an incident response plan that provides a high-level approach for how the incident response capability fits into the overall organization. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8 | ARC-AMPE IR-8]

Acme Health shall develop an incident response plan that meets the unique requirements of the organization, which relate to mission, size, structure, and functions. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8 | ARC-AMPE IR-8]

Acme Health shall develop an incident response plan that defines reportable incidents. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8 | ARC-AMPE IR-8]

Acme Health shall develop an incident response plan that provides metrics for measuring the incident response capability within the organization. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8 | ARC-AMPE IR-8]

Acme Health shall develop an incident response plan that defines the resources and management support needed to effectively maintain and mature an incident response capability. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8 | ARC-AMPE IR-8]

Acme Health shall develop an incident response plan that addresses the sharing of incident information. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8 | ARC-AMPE IR-8]

### 11.2 Plan Review and Approval

Acme Health shall develop an incident response plan that is reviewed and approved by [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8]

Acme Health shall develop an incident response plan that is reviewed and approved by the applicable Information System Security Officer (ISSO) and approved by the Business Owner, at least every one (1) year. [ARC-AMPE IR-8]

Acme Health shall review and update the Incident Response Plan at a minimum every one (1) year or when an incident response event demonstrates a change and/or update is needed to improve the Incident Response Plan. [ARC-AMPE IR-8]

### 11.3 Plan Distribution

Acme Health shall distribute copies of the incident response plan to [Assignment: organization-defined incident response personnel]. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8]

Acme Health shall distribute copies of the incident response plan to all personnel with a role or responsibility for implementing the Incident Response Plan. [ARC-AMPE IR-8]

### 11.4 Plan Updates and Communication

Acme Health shall update the incident response plan to address system and organizational changes or problems encountered during plan implementation, execution, or testing. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8 | ARC-AMPE IR-8]

Acme Health shall communicate incident response plan changes to [Assignment: organization-defined incident response personnel (identified by name and/or by role) and organizational elements]. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8]

Acme Health shall communicate incident response plan changes to all personnel with a role or responsibility for implementing the Incident Response Plan. [ARC-AMPE IR-8]

### 11.5 Plan Protection

Acme Health shall protect the incident response plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification. [NIST 800-53 IR-8 | FedRAMP IR-8 | ARC-AMPE IR-8]

### 11.6 Privacy Incident and Breach Response Plan

Acme Health shall develop and implement a Privacy Incident and Breach Response Plan. [ARC-AMPE IR-8]

Acme Health shall include in the Incident Response Plan for breaches involving Personally Identifiable Information (PII): a process to determine if notice to individuals or other organizations, including oversight organizations, is needed; an assessment process to determine the extent of the harm, embarrassment, inconvenience, or unfairness to affected individuals and any mechanisms to mitigate such harms; and identification of applicable privacy requirements. [NIST 800-53 IR-8(1) | ARC-AMPE IR-8(1)]

## 12. Documentation and Records Management

### 12.1 Policy and Procedure Documentation

Acme Health shall maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with this subpart in written (which may be electronic) form. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(1)]

### 12.2 Action and Assessment Documentation

Acme Health shall maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of actions, activities, or assessments required by this subpart to be documented. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(1)]

### 12.3 Retention

Acme Health shall retain documentation for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(i)]

### 12.4 Availability

Acme Health shall make documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(ii)]

### 12.5 Documentation Review and Update

Acme Health shall review documentation periodically, and update as needed, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of the electronic protected health information. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(iii)]
